As part of this process, PacifiCorp’s distribution engineering team also did an initial analysis of the electrical pathways 9 between the substation and the participating buildings to understand the current state of the voltage, frequency, and capacity for the grind infrastructure. Grid Model. PacifiCorp compiled the utility network (CYME) files for the project locations. The CYME files were extracted in a self-contained data version to include the detailed electrical mapping from the distribution network to the substation, feeders, and participating locations as well as the other distribution parameters. The specific service point locations for the participating buildings were clearly identified for use with the power flow analysis. These files have been reviewed by the project team to determine compatibility for integration into other software tools for network analysis (OpenDSS) and conversions from CYME to OpenDSS were completed. Additionally, SCADA data for each of the substations and feeders were extracted to understand the maximum and minimum loading data for each feeder and location to complete the baseline analysis including power flow analysis, voltage fluctuation analysis, and short circuit analysis for each project location. The grid modelling work was completed for all participating project sites. 6.1.1.4 Subtask 1.4.0: Design Architecture and Communication Pathways Design Architecture. The PacifiCorp project team developed the first iteration of the solution and communication in June 2023, and the initial draft was used for project discussions, DERMS implementation planning, and the first round of the cybersecurity plan. Further discussions were held including meetings with Lawrence Berkeley National Labs as the national coordinator to explain the project solution architecture and document it in a consistent control framework across all the connected communities’ projects. A meeting was held on November 1, 2023, where PacifiCorp presented the project architecture, discussed internal and external systems, covered the existing and planned communication pathways and protocols, and answered questions from other project members and stakeholders. PacifiCorp’s UDERMS iCommunity is currently categorized as a hybrid archetype that leverages both an aggregator and direct building / device integrations. The project team completed preliminary simulation results for this hybrid building level/aggregator DER control archetype to simulate peak load management with DERs including thermostats/HVAC, water heating, solar, EVSE, and battery for all project locations. Communication Pathways. PacifiCorp is focused on using open standard protocols and platforms for communication pathways to support scalability, replicability, and interoperability. To that end, the UDERMS project uses a combination of DNP3 (serial and IP), Open Automated Demand Response (OpenADR) 2.0b, Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP) 1.6, and VOLTTRON. In 2023, PacifiCorp enabled controls with over 100 EVSEs through deployment, testing, and integrations conducted with OCPP 1.6j and OpenADR 2.0b control signals. Detailed unit and field testing was completed to demonstrate field controls of EVSEs. Additionally, testing was done at the USU microgrid facility with the OpenADR lab virtual top node (VTN) communicating to the lab virtual end node (VEN), through OCPP to field EVSE devices.
